memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Israel set out with all that was his, and when he reached Beersheba, he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac." — Gen 46:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob is on the move at last, heading for Egypt to see the son he thought was dead. And at Beersheba he stops.

Beersheba is not a random place. It is where his father Isaac had built an altar and called on the Lord (Gen 26:25), and where God had appeared to Isaac with a promise. It is also the last town before the wilderness — the edge of the promised land. One more step and Jacob leaves behind the country God swore to give his family.

So he pauses, and he worships.

That is worth learning from. Jacob is old, excited, and in a hurry. Joseph had said "don't delay." Everything in him must have wanted to keep moving. Instead he stops at the border and puts God at the centre of the decision.

We are often at our least prayerful precisely when we are most excited. Good news makes us move fast. A new job, a move, a relationship, an opportunity that seems obviously right — and we rush ahead without ever asking God about it. Jacob does the opposite. He brings even his joy to the altar.

Before your next big step, stop where Jacob stopped. Whatever is ahead, God should be consulted before the border is crossed, not after.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you pray as readily about good news as you do about bad news?
2. What decision are you rushing that God is asking you to pause over?
3. Where is your "Beersheba" — a place or habit that helps you refocus on God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for rushing ahead when I am excited and forgetting to bring my plans to You. Teach me to stop and worship before I take the next step. Amen.
